corrections.new: The topic is named without a usable time rule for this scenario. The three periods fixed by the Rules all attach to the registration event rather than to a request for a copy: thirty days from the reporting of the birth to collect a domiciliary extract from the Registrar (Rule 8(2)), thirty days from the event to collect an institutional one from the officer in charge of the institution (Rule 8(4)), which is the hospital-side step this scenario excludes, and a duty on the Registrar or that officer to post an uncollected extract within fifteen days of the expiry of that period (Rule 8(5)), which is triggered automatically and requires no submission by the citizen. The scenario's trigger is a birth already registered where the family now needs a certified copy or a first certificate. For that request no reviewed route gives a processing period, deadline or service-level target: the Greater Chennai Corporation's page carries no timeline text, its download route shows none before the OTP boundary, and the state portal publishes no target for its download and returned HTTP 404 on the download route itself. The three claims are retained as topic-only IDs.

corrections.reason: Understated cell. PROTOCOL section 8 makes time stated when the evidence gives an actionable duration or deadline, and expressly contemplates a figure that covers only one stage: 'when the figure covers only one stage, the cell note must say so'. Rule 8(2), carried by claim_chennai_birth_collect_within_30_days at Grade A, verified, observation, gives a concrete thirty-day deadline for collecting the extract from the Registrar for a domiciliary birth reported directly to the Registrar. The primary scenario covers 'a certified copy or first certificate of a birth already registered', by the municipal civil-registration route, and excludes only hospital-side registration steps, so the Registrar-side collection window is in scope. The absence of a published processing period for a later copy request is a one-stage limitation to be stated in the note, not a reason to record the cell as mentioned.

support.auditNote: Only a verified Grade A claim is relied on, as section 8 requires. The cell note must be re-authored by the official pass to say that the figure covers the collection stage only and that no processing period is published for a later copy request; note text is outside this correction set's field paths.

corrections.reason: Consequential to the state change. A stated cell's claimIds must carry the actionable value, so the four claims the cell's own note rules out of scope cannot remain: claim_chennai_birth_institutional_collect_within_30_days and its second limb govern collection from the officer in charge of the institution, the hospital-side step the primary scenario excludes, and claim_chennai_birth_uncollected_posted_in_fifteen_days and its second limb impose a duty on the Registrar triggered by expiry rather than by anything the citizen submits. claim_chennai_birth_collect_within_30_days_2 names who may collect rather than a duration, so it does not carry the cell's value either. Those periods stay in the ledger and belong in the re-authored cell note as scope limitations.
